correctness.rationale: The common touching point is the only cut point of the Hawaiian earring, so every homeomorphism fixes it and permutes circle petals. Each point on a petal in an infinite permutation orbit has a petal-local wandering neighbourhood; for a finite petal cycle of length q, the return map is a circle homeomorphism fixing the common point. An orientation-preserving circle homeomorphism with a fixed point has nonwandering set exactly its fixed-point set, because a nonfixed interval drifts monotonically; an orientation-reversing return has the corresponding two-step version. Therefore Omega(T)=Per(T), including the common point, for all petal cycles. If all points are periodic, each finite petal-return map is identity or an involution; at each spatial resolution finitely many large petal cycles form an invariant core and the remaining petals have uniformly small diameter, giving two-sided equicontinuity. Conversely, equicontinuity on a compact space excludes wandering points. Equicontinuity forces polynomial entropy zero; any wandering point gives polynomial entropy at least one, and the 2026 regular-curve bound supplies at most one. Hawaiian earring is regular but not a local dendrite; no local-dendrite theorem was misapplied.
residual_risks: Rigidity applies to homeomorphisms of the exact Hawaiian earring; not to arbitrary regular curves or pointwise-periodic continua.
The universal polynomial-entropy upper bound is a cited published theorem, not reproved in the package.

originality.rationale: The inspected full 2026 regular-curve paper bounds entropy by one for all regular curves and treats local dendrites; it explicitly asks about non-local-dendrite regular curves. The Hawaiian earring is not a local dendrite, and the present new step is nonwandering-equals-periodic plus the petal-return criterion, which gives a zero/one dichotomy for this specific continuum. Full 2026 flexibility work constructs different continua with positive entropy despite pointwise periodicity; its examples are not an implication for this space. Naghmouchi 2020 gives nonwandering/recurrent relations but not equality with periodicity on an earring. Best-of-knowledge original as a complete special-space structure result, without claiming an all-regular-curves general theorem.
residual_risks: An unknown earring-specific dynamical classification under other terminology may exist; historical absence is not proven.
The general 2026 pointwise-periodic flexibility examples show that pointwise periodicity alone does not imply zero polynomial entropy on arbitrary continua.

value.rationale: A complete nonwandering, periodicity, return-map and polynomial-entropy classification for the canonical compact regular curve that is not a local dendrite directly addresses the boundary of a 2026 local-dendrite rigidity result. The constructive finite-petal-core argument explains why pointwise periodicity can force equicontinuity here although it cannot on arbitrary continua. This is a motivated structural theorem, not a renamed elementary corollary.
residual_risks: Does not answer the general question for all non-local-dendrite regular curves.

final_claim: On the standard shrinking-circle Hawaiian earring, every homeomorphism has nonwandering set equal to its periodic set. Absence of wandering, pointwise periodicity, two-sided equicontinuity, and zero polynomial entropy are equivalent; otherwise polynomial entropy is one. The precise criterion is determined by the permutation cycles of petals and their circle-return maps (identity for orientation-preserving return; square identity for orientation-reversing return).
limitations: All circles meet at one point and shrink to it; generalized bouquets, nonhomeomorphisms and arbitrary regular curves excluded.
No finite experiment constitutes the topological proof.
